{"id":"f386b566-870b-43ed-836c-b3d4d42df32e","object":"chat.completion","created":1789912539,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"","reasoning_content":"The declared property no_credential_leakage was not discharged. Remove it from the list. Possibly also pii_contained/injection_safe? The veto only flagged no_credential_leakage as failing. Let's remove that one and re-propose. But maybe others also fail one at a time (the veto reports one failing spec at a time?). It says "failing spec: no_credential_leakage". Possibly it reports the first. Safer: trim the list to properties most likely provable and drop the security-flow claims (no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, pii_contained, injection_safe, input_validated) since flow properties may be not_decided when there's no flow at all (no request input used → flow checker has nothing → not_decided rather than proven).

Hmm, but no_secret_leakage wasn't flagged... the flag might be first-failure only. Consider: credential leakage concerns Authorization headers reaching sinks; our handler never touches headers → why would it fail? Perhaps because cacheGet read values are treated as unknown-provenance and reaching the response sink clears no_credential_leakage (like the durable example said: "Reaching the response with that clears the three properties the response sink decides - no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, deterministic"). Yes! In the durable example, waitSignal output is unknown and reaching response clears those three (no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, deterministic) plus idempotent.

And durable example's list: retry_safe, state_isolated, result_safe, optional_safe, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe, canonical, cost_bounded — note input_validated and pii_contained and injection_safe ARE listed even though the value reaches response. Interesting: so it's specifically no_secret_leakage and no_credential_leakage (and deterministic) that get cleared by an unknown value reaching the response sink.

checkAnd cacheGet returns string? — an unknown-provenance value reaching Response.json clears those two as well? It flagged only no_credential_leakage. Perhaps because no_secret_leakage passed... regardless, safest is to drop both no_secret_leakage and no_credential_leakage, and keep the rest (input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe as in durable example).

Should I keep deterministic out? Yes, it's excluded (nondeterministic cache read + cleared).

New list: read_only, state_isolated, retry_safe, optional_safe, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe, canonical, cost_bounded. That mirrors the durable example's set minus result_safe (no Results here) plus read_only.

Hmm, read_only — risky? cacheGet effect read → should hold. Keep, but consider dropping to reduce risk? If read_only were not proven, we'd get another flag. The veto flagged only one failing spec; maybe it flags all? It said "failing spec: no_credential_leakage" singular. So one at a time possibly, or only one truly failing.

I'll keep read_only but drop it if flagged. Actually, to minimize iterations, drop read_only too? Then if it's required/provable, no harm omitting (unless a completeness rule exists — but no evidence of that; the durable example omits properties for stated reasons). Omitting a provable property is safe unless a rule requires it. But the durable example omits deterministic etc. only because they don't hold.

Hmm, read_only is quite likely proven for a handler that only calls a read-effect export. I'll keep it — but risk of another round. Trade-off: keep it; a read-only claim on a read-only handler is honest and likely to pass.

Actually, "retry_safe" — is it proven? Path enumeration based; retry_safe for a read-only handler should hold. Durable example lists it.

cost_bounded: proven presumably (few paths).

Let me propose.","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_00_UG7XhQiny1SUVCR1KOA14268","type":"function","function":{"name":"propose_change_set","arguments":"{"changes": [{"file": "handler.ts", "content": "import { cacheGet } from \"zttp:cache\";\n\nstructural Guard<T> = Proof<T,\n  | \"read_only\"\n  | \"state_isolated\"\n  | \"retry_safe\"\n  | \"optional_safe\"\n  | \"input_validated\"\n  | \"pii_contained\"\n  | \"injection_safe\"\n  | \"canonical\"\n  | \"cost_bounded\"\n>;\n\nexport function handler(req: Request): Guard<Response> {\n  const hits: string = cacheGet(\"counters\", \"hits\") ?? \"0\";\n  return Response.json({ hits: hits });\n}\n"}]}"}}]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":28132,"completion_tokens":1094,"total_tokens":29226,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":27904},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":874},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":27904,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":228},"system_fingerprint":"aeb56401ca74e127821c4f9126dcb669"}
